gloss: to be elegant, to have class, to be refined

definitions.gloss: to be elegant, to have class, to be refined
definitions.explanation: Describes a person, thing, or manner that has an inherent elegance, dignity, or refinement. Used as a compliment for someone or something that exudes good taste and sophistication.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{品|ひん}がある。
{品|ひん}のある{話|はな}し{方|かた}ですね。
examples.english: What an elegant way of speaking.

examples.japanese: この{料亭|りょうてい}は{品|ひん}のある{雰囲気|ふんいき}で、{特別|とくべつ}な{日|ひ}にぴったりだ。
examples.english: This traditional restaurant has a refined atmosphere, making it perfect for special occasions.

notes:
An idiomatic expression built on {品|ひん} (refinement, elegance, class). The negative form {品|ひん}がない means "to lack class" or "to be vulgar." When modifying a noun, the pattern changes to {品|ひん}のある＋noun (e.g., {品|ひん}のある{人|ひと}).

{品|ひん} here refers to an innate quality of grace and good taste, not "goods" or "items" (another meaning of {品|ひん}/{品物|しなもの}).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {品|ひん}がある: to have class/refinement
- {品|ひん}がない: to lack class, to be vulgar
- {品|ひん}のある＋noun: classy/refined + noun
- {品|ひん}のない＋noun: vulgar/classless + noun
- {品|ひん}を{感|かん}じる: to sense elegance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上品|じょうひん}: elegant, refined — a na-adjective with a similar meaning but usable as a standalone modifier
- {気品|きひん}がある: to have dignity/grace — slightly more elevated, often for nobility or royalty
- {品格|ひんかく}がある: to have dignity — focuses more on character and moral refinement
